slides.texte_overlay:
Old school skills that will
make you unforgettable
Learn to write a proper letter. A real one, on paper, for a birthday, a thank you, a goodbye. People keep letters for decades. Nobody has ever kept a text message in a shoebox.
Learn to hold the door and let people go first. Not as a show. Just because it's kind. It costs one second, and in a world where everyone rushes, people remember the guy who didn't.
Know a little about a lot. Five minutes a day of history, art or science, and you've always got a good story at dinner. Old school people were curious about everything. Be like them.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Now I've always got a good story at dinner. Old school people were curious about everything.

slides.texte_overlay: Learn to call instead of texting for the important stuff. Birthdays, bad news, good news. Hearing your voice means something. A call that lasts two minutes beats a hundred messages with emojis.
Learn to dress for the occasion. A clean shirt for dinner at her parents' place, a jacket for a wedding, no sneakers at a funeral. Showing up dressed right is a quiet way of saying "I respect this."
Learn to remember birthdays without your phone reminding you. Write them in a small notebook. A message that shows up on the right day, with no reminder at all, feels genuinely thoughtful.

Learn to bring something when you visit. Flowers for the host, a bottle for dinner, pastries on a Sunday. It's an old habit that never stopped working. People always remember who showed up thoughtful.
